recent_posts.title: Qt Design Studio 4.8.2 Released
recent_posts.summary: Qt Design Studio 4.8.2 introduces a fully agentic AI assistant built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Unlike the prompt-based beta in 4.8.1, the rebuilt assistant understands entire project structures and can autonomously read files, create components, and modify existing ones in an iterative loop. It supports models from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, with the ability to switch providers mid-conversation. The release also bumps the bundled Qt Kit from 6.8.5 to 6.8.6.

recent_posts.title: Introducing the QML Profiler Skill for Agentic Development
recent_posts.summary: The Qt Company has introduced a QML Profiler Skill for agentic development that lets AI agents handle performance profiling of Qt Quick 2D applications. The skill automates the full profiling workflow: locating Qt tools, enabling QML debugging, running the profiler in one of four modes (full, rendering, logic, memory), parsing the resulting .qtd trace file with a bundled Python parser, identifying hotspots mapped back to source code, and generating a timestamped Markdown report with frame-time percentiles, memory breakdowns, and specific fix suggestions. It works with Claude Code CLI, Claude Desktop, and GitHub Copilot in VS Code, and supports models like Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT 5.4, and Gemini 3.1 Pro. Limitations include no support for Qt Quick 3D, GPU-side costs, C++ backend profiling, or hardware-specific optimizations. The skill is available on GitHub and Claude's marketplace under the 'qt-development' plugin.

recent_posts.title: Introducing the Qt Code Review Skills for Agentic Development
recent_posts.summary: Qt Code Review Skills are AI-powered agent tools for automated code quality analysis of Qt6 C++ and QML codebases. The workflow runs a deterministic Python linter (60+ C++ rules, 47+ QML checks) followed by six parallel deep-analysis agents covering areas like memory ownership, thread safety, binding loops, and performance anti-patterns. Only findings above an 80/100 confidence threshold are reported as confirmed issues. The skills are read-only, require Python 3 and optionally Git or qmllint, and have been tested with Claude Code CLI, GitHub Copilot, and frontier models like GPT and Gemini. Available via a GitHub repository and soon as a Claude marketplace plugin.

recent_posts.title: Using the WebView module with C++ and Qt Widgets
recent_posts.summary: Qt 6.11 introduces a C++ API for the Qt WebView module under Technology Preview, giving C++ developers an alternative to Qt WebEngine for embedding web content. Unlike WebEngine, which bundles a full Chromium runtime, WebView wraps the system-provided web libraries (Edge WebView2 on Windows, WkWebView on macOS/iOS, Android WebView), reducing resource usage and binary size. The QWebView class subclasses QWindow, and can be embedded in Qt Widgets apps via QWidget::createWindowContainer(). The API supports navigation controls, JavaScript injection with result callbacks, load status signals, and per-instance settings via a WebAttribute enumeration. The Qt team is seeking developer feedback before finalizing the API.

recent_posts.title: Security advisory: QML Code Injection in VectorImage Component in Qt declarative module impacts Qt
recent_posts.summary: A code injection vulnerability (CVE-2025-14576) has been discovered in the VectorImage component of Qt's declarative module. Insufficient validation of node IDs in SVG files allows a malicious SVG to inject and execute arbitrary QML/JavaScript code within the application context. The vulnerability affects Qt 6.8.0–6.8.6 and Qt 6.9.0–6.10.1 across all major platforms and architectures, with a CVSS 4.0 score of 7.4 (HIGH). Potential impacts include denial of service, information disclosure, and other effects depending on application privileges. The fix is to update to Qt 6.8.7 or Qt 6.10.2 or later, or apply the provided patches. As a mitigation, only load SVG files from trusted sources and validate/sanitize SVG content before loading.

recent_posts.title: Qt Contributors Summit 2026: Oslo in October!
recent_posts.summary: The Qt Contributors Summit 2026 is scheduled for October 28-29 in Oslo, Norway, hosted by reMarkable. The event expands into a full 'week of Qt in Oslo' running October 27-30, including a Qt World Summit 2026 viewing on the 27th, a welcome evening event, two days of discussions and workshops, and a Friday hackathon on the 30th. The summit is open to maintainers, contributors, and Qt enthusiasts.

recent_posts.title: Figma to Qt 1.0 converts Figma designs directly to QML without leaving Figma
recent_posts.summary: Figma to Qt 1.0 is now available as a free Figma plugin that converts GUI designs directly into QML code without leaving Figma. Unlike extraction-based tools, it runs inside Figma and provides a live browser preview of the Qt interface during design iteration. Key features include an issues tab that flags QML incompatibilities early, support for Qt Quick Controls components (buttons, sliders, checkboxes, etc.), global shared Figma library support, and export as a complete QML project zip. It replaces Qt Bridge for Figma, removing the Qt Design Studio intermediary step and generating cleaner, more faithful QML directly for use in Qt Creator, VS Code, or Qt Design Studio.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Qt Agentic Development Skills
recent_posts.summary: Qt Company is releasing a set of agentic development skills for Qt C++ and QML codebases. The skills include a multi-layered code review tool that runs a deterministic linter across 60+ rules plus up to six parallel sub-agents checking areas like memory ownership, thread safety, and performance. A documentation skill auto-generates structured Markdown reference docs for components. A QML Coding Skill applies best practices during code generation rather than after, achieving up to 11% better QML code quality on the QML100 benchmark. All skills work with Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and other agentic tools, and are available via a GitHub repository or Claude's marketplace.

recent_posts.title: Qt Safe Renderer 2.2 Release Candidate 2 Released
recent_posts.summary: Qt Safe Renderer 2.2 Release Candidate 2 is now available for commercial license holders. It includes bug fixes and documentation improvements over RC1, and ships with prebuilt binaries for Qt 6.8.7. The release enables safety-critical UI items in Qt Quick Ultralite applications and is intended for use alongside Qt for MCUs 2.12. It is available via the Qt Online Installer but has not yet been certified.

recent_posts.title: Qt for MCUs 2.12.1 LTS and Updates
recent_posts.summary: Qt for MCUs 2.12.1 LTS is a patch release with bug fixes and several notable additions. New platform support includes Infineon PSOC Edge E84 SoC as an official Tier-2 package and STM32N6 microcontrollers as Tier-3. A visual log analyzer technology preview enables performance monitoring via serial port. Deep sleep mode support is added for Infineon TRAVEO T2G MCUs, enabling power-optimized use cases like smartwatches. The Coco code coverage tool now supports Qt for MCUs with pre-configured compiler profiles and merged C++/QML coverage results. A sneak peek at a dynamic applet ecosystem — allowing app installation on a running MCU without full flash replacement — was also showcased.

top_posts.title: Atomic Design Systems: Why the Labels Don’t Matter
top_posts.summary: Atomic design remains relevant in 2025, but not through rigid chemistry labels. The methodology's creator, Brad Frost, confirms the labels were never the point—hierarchical composition is. Modern design systems should use semantic, purpose-driven naming (like Modal.Warning.SpeedLimit instead of Organism_7) that communicates intent clearly. Design tokens have become the essential foundation layer, providing single sources of truth for colors, spacing, and typography. Templates and pages remain valuable for maintaining layout consistency. The key is building systems that help teams create better products faster, not debating whether components are atoms or molecules.

top_posts.title: GUI for Embedded Applications: Expert Design Insights & Trends
top_posts.summary: Four industry veterans with 60+ years of combined experience discuss the evolution, challenges, and future of GUI design for embedded systems. Key insights include how user expectations have matured over 20 years, the shift from Photoshop to Figma and AI-assisted tools, and fundamental differences between web and embedded design (hardware constraints, safety criticality, unique contexts). The panel emphasizes that timeless design principles remain constant despite technological change, highlights the importance of designer-developer collaboration from day one, and views AI as an accelerator rather than replacement for human expertise. Current trends include larger typography, dark mode theming, micro-animations, and 2.5D layering effects that balance visual appeal with performance constraints.

top_posts.title: Qt 6.10 Released!
top_posts.summary: Qt 6.10 introduces a flexbox layout system for responsive UIs, animated vector graphics support for SVG and Lottie formats, and a new SearchField control. The release simplifies C++ to QML data integration with QRangeModel for exposing C++ ranges to item views, delegateModelAccess for two-way bindings, and TreeModel for declarative tree structures. Accessibility improvements include automatic high-contrast mode support across platforms. Android developers get official support for Android 15/16, Qt Jenny 1.0 for JNI code generation, and improved splash screen handling. The release adds macOS 26 support, WebView2 backend for Qt WebView on Windows, and PipeWire support for Qt Multimedia on Linux.

top_posts.title: Examples of local LLM usage
top_posts.summary: The post outlines how to use local large language models (LLMs) on a MacBook Pro M1 Max for generating images, extracting text from audio, and summarizing text. The author describes the use of stable-diffusion.cpp for image generation, whisper.cpp for audio transcription, and llama.cpp for text summarization. Detailed scripts and time performance metrics are provided for each use case.

top_posts.title: Qt on macOS 26 Tahoe
top_posts.summary: Qt framework announces compatibility preparations for macOS 26 Tahoe, addressing challenges with the new Liquid Glass design system. The team has updated their Apple platform support policy to clarify forward compatibility and provides workaround mechanisms for applications experiencing styling issues. Qt continues working on enabling liquid glass effects in their native styles while maintaining compatibility mode options for existing applications.
